resolutions.fix: The widening branch was rejected with a reason: an extract is the attempt that COMPLETES a recovery, recovery-replan-postcondition is the shape where the replan is nothing but an extract, and forbidding it the label would make recovery_verified 0/1 there and turn that case red. The metric's question is not 'does this step change the page' but 'could this step have saved the run' — an observe produces no answer, an extract does. specs/001-browser-contract.md and ADR-019 section 2 now say that.

T-M32-3 now states the true cost model: only a postcondition failure pays SETTLE_BUDGET_MS; an act failure raised inside execute never reaches check_state. The cheap design was also taken — shop.html's search box gets the maxlength every real search box has, so a too-long fill is truncated and the readback check raises instantly. R8's case costs 0.15s where the reviewer's click-timeout repro costs 10.9s.

case_redundancy_review.question: Whether one of the three laundering cases became redundant once the cheap shape existed.
case_redundancy_review.answer: CORRECTED by PR #34 R13. The claim as first written — that the three cases pin three distinct shapes — described the INPUTS the three cases drive, and asserted of the ASSERTIONS something that was not true of them. `observe-cannot-launder-noop-action` asserted only `failure:act` plus `recovery: false`, and the drill-down guard reaches that identical terminal status on that identical input one step later, so the case stayed green with family 2's guard replaced by `elif False:` and the whole fast suite stayed green (131/131 on the merged tree) with `reads_without_acting` reverted to its pre-R1 one-liner — the PR #34 R1 fix had no coverage anywhere. The round-2 answer below was not checked by mutation, and stating it as though it had been is the part of R13 that is about this artifact rather than about the code. What is true NOW: the three inputs remain distinct as described, and the assertions distinguish them — `observe-cannot-launder-noop-action` also asserts `trace_actions: [navigate, click]` and `replans: 0`, so a refusal at replan time is separable from a refusal after the observation was taken, and both mutations were watched red before the assertion landed.
case_redundancy_review.original_answer_round_2: No. The three pin three distinct shapes and each triage note says which — family 2's guard with page_changed: false; the drill-down guard with page_changed: false (reached through a replan that legitimately acts); the drill-down guard with page_changed: null, which neither of the others can produce because both of theirs fail a postcondition rather than raising inside execute. Pinning only one of the two values is precisely how R8 happened, so neither was traded away for wall clock.
